_comment: Shared truth for the unlock-pattern canonicalizer, which is duplicated in
Both test suites read this file, so if the two copies ever drift the suites
fail instead of silently minting a hash nobody can log in with.
Cells are indexed row-major over a 3x3 grid: 0 1 2 / 3 4 5 / 6 7 8.
_countsComment: Reachable pattern counts per length, under Android's rule that a straight
move may not skip over an unvisited cell. Enumerated by DFS in the specs;
these match the published Android figures (total 4..9 = 389,112).
Requiring 6 cells keeps 380,336 of them - only 2.26% of the space is lost,
but every short, human-favoured pattern goes with it.
_intermediatesComment: The only eight ordered pairs (plus their reverses) that pass over a third
cell. A midpoint exists iff the row sum and the column sum are both even.
_noIntermediateComment: Adjacent moves and knight-moves obstruct nothing. Knight-moves are the
interesting case: 0 -> 5 must stay legal even with 1, 2 and 4 unvisited.
_canonicalComment: `taps` is the raw sequence of cells the finger lands on; `canonical` is the
string that gets bcrypt-hashed. The gap between the two is the skip rule.

canonical.name: top-row drag inserts 1; the long diagonals insert 4 and 7
passing back over an already-visited cell does not re-add it
knight moves never insert a cell
re-touching the cell under the finger is ignored
visiting the centre first makes both long diagonals legal
